name: Brachyolmia Type 1, Toledo Type

ethnicAssociations: Reported in diverse populations, initially described in Toledo, Spain

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Brachyolmia Type 1

criteria.description: Presence of disproportionate short trunk dwarfism with normal limb length
Radiological evidence of platyspondyly (flattened vertebral bodies) throughout the spine
Identification of pathogenic variants in the PAPSS2 gene associated with Toledo type
Mild shortening of long bones without significant metaphyseal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of disproportionate short trunk dwarfism, platyspondyly on imaging, and pathogenic PAPSS2 gene variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical-radiological correlation and genetic testing; exclusion of other skeletal dysplasias is essential.

common.symptomName: Mild short stature with normal limb proportions
searchTerms: slightly short height with normal limbs
mild short stature with proportional limbs
small overall height but normal limb size

rare.notes: May cause neurological symptoms if present
searchTerms: tight spinal canal causing nerve issues

imaging: Platyspondyly with flattened vertebral bodies on spine X-rays
Mild metaphyseal irregularities on long bone radiographs
genetic: Pathogenic variants in PAPSS2 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Normal cognitive function on neurodevelopmental assessment

distinguishingFeatures: More severe vertebral and metaphyseal abnormalities
Earlier onset and more pronounced short stature
Involvement of epiphyses with delayed ossification
Severe short stature with short limbs

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits suggesting spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic insufficiency
Rapid progression of skeletal deformities beyond typical phenotype
